content:
For even \(N\), use these representations:

- If \(N\equiv 0 \pmod 6\) and \(N\ge 18\), then
  \[
  N=9+(N-9),
  \]
  where \(N-9\) is an odd composite multiple of \(3\).

- If \(N\equiv 4 \pmod 6\) and \(N\ge 34\), then
  \[
  N=25+(N-25),
  \]
  where \(N-25\) is an odd composite multiple of \(3\).

- If \(N\equiv 2 \pmod 6\) and \(N\ge 44\), then
  \[
  N=35+(N-35),
  \]
  where \(N-35\) is an odd composite multiple of \(3\).

Thus every even \(N\ge 40\) is representable.

Now check \(38\): the odd composites below \(38\) are
\[
9,15,21,25,27,33,35.
\]
Their complements are
\[
29,23,17,13,11,5,3,
\]
all prime. So \(38\) cannot be expressed as the sum of two composite odd positive integers.

\[
\boxed{38}
\]
